newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NZ's Peters says budget on track despite GDP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NZ's Peters says budget on track despite GDP.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday that forecasts in the government's 1997/98 budget were not endangered by low March quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data.

"No I don't," Peters told reporters after a luncheon address to the Trans-Tasman Business Circle when asked if the 0.5 percent contraction in March quarter GDP had slowed the expected growth path and affected the government's forecasts of surpluses in the next two years.
"I think there's been a turnaround even since the budget in business confidence," he said.
"A significant number of businesses and business opinion had a certain view as to who should run the economy -- they're coming to grips with political reality under MMP," he said.

The current coalition government of Peters' New Zealand First party and the conservative National party was formed after the 1996 election, the first under the Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) voting system which tends to deliver coalitions.
"You're talking about a GDP (growth rate) of about 2.2-2.3 percent at the very bottom of the trough -- that's a pretty good trough when you look at it that way," he said.
Peters said economy had been falling since March last year and the economy was now back onto a more optimistic growth path.
The government forecasts a budget operating surplus of NZ$1.5 billion for the year to June 30, 1998, rising to NZ$1.9 billion in 1998/99.
Economists, however, have expressed doubt about the viability of the budget forecasts since the release of the surprisingly weak growth figures.
